sentences.text: 2. Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.

4. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 07-01-2013 at about 12-40 PM the petitioner along with her father-in-law and son were proceeding in their own Maruti Swift Car bearing Reg. No. KA-04/MJ-5510 to go to Gotur for attending in engagement ceremony, when the vehicle is on Gulbarga Main Road at Aurad (B) village, at that time one Cruiser Jeep bearing Reg.

No.AP-11/W-8061 came from opposite side in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner on wrong route and dashed to the right side of Car, due to which petitioners were injured grievously to her head, hands and pubic rami and other parts of the body.

Immediately she and other injured persons were shifted to Basaveshwar Hospital, Gulbarga & after knowing the severity of injuries she has shifted to Uday Clinic Hyderabad Hospital for treatment on 08-01-2013 and she has been treated as inpatient and operated to injuries.

Prior to the accident the petitioner is aged about 28 years and she was hale and healthy and was doing Tailoring Work and earning more than Rs.
10,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, the petitioner cannot work as early and she was permanently disabled to do any work.
The Respondent No. 1 is businessman, respondent No.2 is the insurer to the offending vehicle.
Hence, he preferred a claim petition seeking compensation.

5. After service of notice, through respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through their counsel, only respondent No.2 has filed written statement denying the contents of claim made by the petitioner and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

7. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and also examined the Doctor as PW.2 and two more witnesses as PW3 and 4 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P20.
On the other hand, the respondent counsel have not adduced any oral evidence, but cop of the insurance policy is produced which is marked as Ex.R1 with consent of the petitioner's counsel.

2 8.

The Tribunal, after recording the evidence and considering the material on record, allowed the petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.5,24,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till date of deposit and held that respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation and directed the respondent No.2 to deposit the compensation amount.
Being dissatisfied with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner has filed the present appeal seeking for enhancement of compensation amount.

9. Heard the learned counsel for petitioner and learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company.
10.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the compensation awarded by the tribunal is on the lower side.
The tribunal has committed an error in taking notional income of Rs.6000/- instead of Rs.7000/- as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.

Further it is submitted that as per the evidence of doctor-PW2, he has issued disability certificate-Ex.P.8 of the petitioner to the whole body is 30% but the tribunal has taken only 20% to the whole body.
The tribunal has not awarded any amount for future medical expense and towards other heads also the tribunal has awarded meager compensation and seeks for enhancement.
On these grounds learned counsel seeks indulgence of this Court to allow the appeal and consequently seeks to enhance the compensation.
11. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2/Insurance Company supports the judgment and award passed by the tribunal and does not call for any interference.
Hence, prays to dismiss the appeal.

12. Perused the records and considered the submission made by the learned counsel for the parties.
13.
The point that arise for consideration is with regard to quantum of compensation.

14. With regard to loss of future income is concerned, the tribunal has observed in pg.No.17 of the impugned judgment as under:
(V) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:
The petitioner has contended that she is age of 28 years.
The age of the petitioner is mentioned as 30 years in wound certificate.
Therefore the age of the petitioner is considered as 30 years as on date of accident.
However on considering the entire evidence it can be come to conclusion that the petitioner age is 30 years.
The petitioner contended that she has sustained grievous injuries and total disability 60%.
In support of the petitioner contention, she has produced disability certificate, which is marked as Ex.P.8.
The Doctor also examined as PW2.
As per Ex.P.8 the disability of the petitioner to whole body is 35%.

As per X-Ray report evidence of old malunited fracture of right iliac bone with internal fixation screws seen in situ and evidence of old mal united fracture of superior and inferior and inferior rami of Right pubic bone.

On considering the entire evidence of medical report and the nature of injury, the disability of 35% as stated by the Doctor is higher side and the disability is Savita vs Sangameshwar And Anr on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138945408/
3 considered only 20% to whole body.

The petitioner in the petition stated that she is doing Tailor work and earning a sum of Rs. 10,000/-
per month.
In support of her contention the petitioner has not produced any document..
In the absence of such document, it cannot be said that the income of the petitioner is Rs.10,000/- per month.
Hence, it is just and proper to consider the notional income of the petitioner and accordingly I hold that the income of the petitioner is Rs.6,000/- per month as she being a housewife.
Therefore the monthly income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.6,000/-.

As per the guidelines of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarala Verma and others /Vs/ Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier is applicable to age between 26 to 30 is 17.

Therefore the petitioner is entitle compensation of (6,000 x 12 x 17 x 20)/ 100)
Rs.2,44,800/-.
15.

Considering the medical evidence and nature and gravity of injuries and also evidence of Pw1-Savitha and PW5-Dr. Ramakanth Kulkarni, it is just and proper to assess disability to the whole body at 25%.
16. The petitioner has not produced any evidence with regard to his income.
Therefore, the notional income has to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Since the accident has taken place in the year 2013, the notional income has to be taken at Rs.7,000/- p.m.
The petitioner is aged about 28 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '17'.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,57,000/-
(Rs.7,000/- x 12 x 17 x 25%) on account of 'loss of future income'.
17.

Towards loss of pain and suffering is concerned in para No.1 of page No.16, the tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering but while calculating the amount in page No.19,
the amount is - 10 - shown as Rs.30,000/-, which is not just and proper.

Hence, the appellant is entitled for Rs.50,000/-
towards pain and suffering.
18. Towards medical expanses is concerned, the tribunal has awarded Rs.2,07,241/- and that there is no need to interfere in this regard and the same is rounded of to Rs.2,08,000/-.
19. Towards attendant, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges
, the tribunal has awarded Rs.14,000/-, which is not just and proper.

Considering the nature of injuries, period of taking treatment and occupation, it is just and proper to award an amount of Rs.30,000/- and it is accordingly awarded.
20.
Towards loss of amenities and nutrition food is concerned the tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/-.

Considering the nature of injury, occupation, medical evidence, it is just and proper to Savita vs Sangameshwar And Anr on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138945408/
4 award compensation of Rs.35,000/-.
Loss of income during treatment is concerned, tribunal has awarded Rs.18,000/- which is enhanced to Rs.30,000/-.

22. With regard to future medical expenses is concerned, it is brought to the notice of this court that the PW.5-Dr.Ramakanth Kilkarni has clearly stated that as per X-ray report evidence of old malunited fracture of right iliac bone with internal fixation screws seen in situ and evidence of old mal united fracture of superior and inferior and inferior rami of right public bone and that the claimant may under go screw removal and he assessed about Rs.70,000/- to Rs.80,000/-
approximately is required for future medical expense.
The tribunal has not assigned any reasons for not awarding compensation towards future medical expanse.
23. The learned counsel for the respondent has submitted her argument that PW2 is not a treated doctor and no estimation is given by the treated doctor as to the future medical expanses.
Hence, the tribunal has not - 12 - passed any award in this regard.

But considering the nature of injury, occupation, medical evidence,
it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards future medical expanses.

24. Hence, this Court re-assesses the compensation on the following heads;

1. Towards Pain & Rs.30,000/- R.50,000/-
suffering 2.

Towards Medical Rs.2,07,241/- Rs.2,08,000/-.
expenses

3. Towards future income Rs.2,44,800/- Rs.3,57,000/-
4. Towards attendant's Rs.14,000/- Rs.30,000/-

The petitioner is entitled for the total compensation of Rs.7,50,000/- as against Rs.5,24,000/- awarded by the tribunal.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled - 13 - for enhanced compensation of Rs.7,50,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
26.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
(a) The appeal is allowed in part.
(b) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.
The petitioner is entitled for the total compensation of Rs. Rs.7,50,000/- as against Rs.5,24,000/- awarded by the tribunal.

(c) The petitioner is entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.7,50,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization except on Rs.40,000/- awarded towards future medical expanses.

(d) The respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation amount before the tribunal within a period of eight - 14 - weeks from date of the receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
